period_policy: User selected latest complete month versus preceding month. Verify statement coverage before assigning the evaluation period; activity dates alone are insufficient.
data_policy: User authorized anonymized real-data context through OpenRouter. Exclude user names, account names/numbers, IDs, raw descriptions and other identifiers. Use local aliases for contributors/merchants. Keep financial fixtures and reports outside version control; no private records in this public catalog.

questions: Explain my income for the latest complete month in my records.
Why does it differ from the preceding month? Compare the same definition of income.
What are the top contributors to the change?
How many refunds did I receive, how much were they, and who were they from?
reference_requirements: Monthly earned income and other income separately
Current/prior contributor totals and signed deltas
Refund count and sum by anonymized merchant
hard_checks: Refunds and internal transfers are not earned income
Rank change contributors by absolute delta with direction
Do not describe all positive credits as salary

questions: Explain my spending for the latest complete month.
What are my largest spending categories and merchants?
How did they change from the preceding month?
What patterns does the available history suggest? Distinguish recent changes from things that persist, and avoid guessing about my lifestyle.
reference_requirements: Gross purchases, refunds, and net spending separately
hard_checks: Exclude own-account transfers and duplicate card payments
No sensitive or unsupported lifestyle inference
Do not call a one-month observation persistent

questions: Is there a spending surge in a category or at a particular merchant that I should notice?
How much did it increase, and what baseline are you comparing it with?
Is this a one-off purchase, repeated activity, or something you cannot determine?
What would you check before deciding this needs action?
reference_requirements: Category/merchant history with counts, amounts and coverage
hard_checks: Report absolute change alongside percentage
No percentage growth from a zero baseline
Do not label unusual spending as fraud without evidence

questions: How did my total wealth change over the comparison period?
How much can be explained by salary and spending, versus investment performance?
How much less or more did I spend than in the preceding period? Do not count that change twice.
Show what reconciles to the total wealth change and what remains unexplained.
reference_requirements: Dividends, interest, fees and valuation changes
hard_checks: Own-account investment contributions do not increase consolidated wealth
Spending reductions are a counterfactual comparison, not an extra inflow
Do not infer gains from balance changes alone
Disclose incomplete valuation coverage

questions: How am I doing financially compared with people earning a similar salary? Do you actually have suitable comparison data?
What can you assess from my own records without inventing a peer ranking?
How much did I transfer into and out of my investment portfolio each month?
How much did I save each month, and how is that different from investment contributions?
reference_requirements: Monthly income, net spending, money retained and savings rate
Gross portfolio inflows/outflows and net contributions
Explicit peer benchmark availability flag; default unavailable
hard_checks: No invented peer percentile or benchmark
Salary alone does not define comparable households
Investment transfers are not additional savings
Savings rate unavailable when denominator is zero

questions: How would you describe my investment style based on my actual holdings and activity?
What evidence supports that description, and what can you not infer?
Did interest and dividends contribute more than price appreciation over this period?
Separate distributions, realized gains, unrealized gains, contributions and fees where the data supports it.
hard_checks: Do not infer personality or risk tolerance from holdings alone
Reinvested dividends counted once
Lifetime unrealized gains are not period gains
No performance attribution without adequate basis and period data

questions: How much money moved into and out of my accounts during the period?
Separate transfers between my own accounts from money entering or leaving my finances.
Which recurring transfer routes or timing patterns are visible?
Are there unmatched or unusual transfers I should review, and why?
reference_requirements: Confirmed transfer pairs and unresolved candidates
Internal movement counted once per pair
hard_checks: Do not double-count the two legs of an internal transfer
Unmatched does not automatically mean external
Do not claim fraud from a timing or amount anomaly
State the scope of every transfer total

required_harness_extensions: Frozen independently checked references for each conversation; do not fabricate expected numeric values
Structured named-entity and behavioral checks beyond numeric claim extraction
Separate unsupported-inference, uncertainty, and benchmark-availability gates
Memory acquisition/probe cases before making memory-improvement claims
Fresh held-out conversations not used for optimization
